title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Releases ‘Dancing with Joy’, an Inspirational Memoir by Dr. Ananda Shankar Jayant
subtitle:
Awareness, Early Detection and Timely Treatment Are Key to Saving Lives from Cancer: Vice-President

Expansion of Cancer Care Facilities Is Bringing Specialised Treatment Closer to Patients: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today released Dancing with Joy, an inspirational memoir by renowned classical dancer, author and former Indian Railway Traffic Service officer Dr. Ananda Shankar Jayant, at Uprashtrapathi Bhavan.
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President described the book as much more than a story about dance and joy, calling it a powerful account of passion, hard work, resilience and the extraordinary strength that comes from discovering and nurturing one’s talent.
Highlighting the book’s account of Dr. Ananda Shankar Jayant’s journey through cancer, the Vice-President said that it was not merely a book about cancer, but a story of life beyond cancer. He observed that a deeply nurtured passion could become an anchor during life’s most difficult moments and help transform adversity into an opportunity for self-discovery.
Referring to the book’s message that the ‘D’ in DANCER helped its author overcome the ‘C’ in cancer, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that dance, nurtured through years of discipline, learning and dedication, had become Dr. Ananda’s core strength in confronting one of life’s greatest challenges.
The Vice-President highlighted that, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Bharat is strengthening preventive healthcare, awareness and early screening through initiatives such as Ayushman Arogya Mandirs and the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases. He noted that the expansion of cancer care facilities across States was bringing specialised treatment closer to patients, with over 700 District Clinics and 500 Day Care Cancer Centres established, and 19 State Cancer Institutes and 20 Tertiary Care Cancer Centres approved for operationalisation. He also highlighted the ₹5 lakh annual health coverage for eligible families under Ayushman Bharat and the nationwide HPV vaccination campaign launched in February 2026, which aims to protect approximately 1.2 crore young girls against cervical cancer, with over 50 lakh girls already vaccinated.
Drawing lessons from Dr. Ananda’s experience, the Vice-President said that success and failure were two sides of the same coin and that every setback offered an opportunity to learn, reflect and return with renewed determination. He urged people facing cancer and other serious challenges not to lose hope, emphasising the importance of courage and a positive mindset.He emphasised that awareness, early detection and timely treatment could save lives.
The Vice-President also acknowledged the vital role played by families and volunteers in supporting cancer patients. He observed that families provided essential emotional strength, encouragement and care during the most difficult phases of a patient’s life, often making considerable personal and financial sacrifices.
The Vice-President said that talent, while a gift, could be transformed into excellence only through sustained learning, practice and commitment. He observed that passion was not a luxury but a source of strength, and that the abilities and interests nurtured during ordinary times could become invaluable resources when extraordinary challenges arose.
Congratulating Dr. Ananda Shankar Jayant on the publication, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan expressed the hope that 'Dancing with Joy' would inspire young people to discover and develop their talents, touch countless lives and remind readers that, whatever rhythm life offered, it was possible to meet it with courage, grace and joy.
Chairman, Sangeet Natak Akademi, Dr. Sandhya Purecha; Chairman, Ushalakshmi Breast Cancer Foundation, Dr. P. Raghu Ram; and Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi, were among the dignitaries present on the occasion. Doctors, cancer specialists and cancer survivors also attended the event.

title: PM to Inaugurate and Dedicate Five Development Projects Worth Around ₹3,350 Crore in Ladakh on 15 October
subtitle:
Projects Span Airport Infrastructure, Strategic Road Connectivity, Hydropower, Heritage Conservation and Water Security

PM to Inaugurate New Passenger Terminal Building at Leh Airport

PM to Dedicate 298-km Nimmu-Padum-Darcha Road, Providing Alternative Connectivity to Ladakh and Strengthening Strategic Mobility for the Armed Forces

PM to Inaugurate India’s First Petroglyph Conservation Park in Leh for Preservation of Ladakh’s Ancient Archaeological Heritage
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 3:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate and dedicate to the nation five major development projects worth around ₹3,350 crore in Ladakh on 15 October 2026 at around 12:30 PM via video conferencing. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The five projects will strengthen connectivity, improve energy infrastructure, conserve cultural heritage and enhance water security in the region.
Prime Minister will inaugurate the New Passenger Terminal Building at Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport, Leh, built at a cost of ₹640 crore. Spread over 23,800 square metres, the modern terminal is designed to handle 35 lakh passengers annually. Incorporating geothermal energy to enhance energy efficiency and reduce its carbon footprint, the facility reflects the importance of sustainable infrastructure in Ladakh’s ecologically sensitive environment. Blending modern passenger amenities with elements of Ladakh’s rich cultural heritage, the terminal will improve passenger convenience and strengthen air connectivity with the rest of the country.
Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation the 298-km-long Nimmu-Padum-Darcha Road, constructed by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO). Connecting Nimmu in Leh with Darcha in Himachal Pradesh through the remote Zanskar Valley, the road provides an alternative connectivity corridor to Ladakh, supplementing the Srinagar–Leh and Manali–Leh highways. Traversing challenging Himalayan terrain, including the high-altitude Shinkun La Pass, the road marks a significant engineering achievement. Its strategic importance lies in enhancing operational mobility and strengthening logistical support for the Armed Forces. It will also benefit residents of Zanskar by improving access to healthcare, education, markets and essential services.
As part of efforts to strengthen energy security and harness Ladakh’s renewable energy potential, Prime Minister will inaugurate the 9 MW Hanu Small Hydroelectric Project and the 66 kV Double-Circuit Dah-Hanu-Khaltsi Transmission Line. The projects will strengthen power evacuation infrastructure and improve the reliability of Ladakh’s electricity network. They mark an important step towards harnessing the region’s hydropower resources and strengthening its energy infrastructure.
Recognising the importance of preserving Ladakh’s ancient archaeological heritage, Prime Minister will inaugurate India’s first Petroglyph Conservation Park at Sindhu Ghat, Leh. Ladakh is home to hundreds of prehistoric rock art sites featuring carvings of wildlife, human figures and symbolic representations that offer valuable insights into thousands of years of human history. These petroglyphs are an irreplaceable record of the region’s cultural and civilisational past. The conservation park will provide a dedicated space for protecting these vulnerable archaeological remains, raising public awareness and encouraging responsible heritage tourism.
Prime Minister will also inaugurate 40 water bodies developed across 40 villages under Project Him Sarovar, an initiative aimed at addressing Ladakh’s unique geographical and climatic challenges through water conservation, in line with the objectives of Mission Amrit Sarovar. Agriculture in Ladakh faces a seasonal imbalance between water availability and demand. Farmers often experience water scarcity during the crucial sowing season, even as snowmelt and glacial runoff provide substantial water resources during other periods. Project Him Sarovar seeks to address this challenge by conserving water when it is available and ensuring its availability when required, thereby supporting irrigation, sustaining agricultural livelihoods and strengthening long-term water security in the region.

title: Government Approves Strategic Restructuring of IDBI Bank Ltd.
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
IDBI Bank Ltd. is a scheduled commercial bank regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Due to its poor financial health, the Bank required repeated infusion of capital, initially provided by the Government of India and later by the LIC. On 5th May, 2017, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) put the IDBI Bank under the Prompt Corrective Action Framework and imposed several restrictions in view of its non-performing assets and losses incurred by the Bank. After considering the improvement in the Bank’s financial health, the RBI later, vide its letter dated 10th March, 2021, lifted the restrictions imposed on the IDBI Bank subject to certain conditions and continuous monitoring.
It was against this backdrop that the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved strategic restructuring of the IDBI Bank Ltd., and in compliance thereof, it was decided that an aggregate 60.72% of the equity stake in the IDBI Bank Ltd be sold to a Strategic Buyer, of which, the GoI share would be 30.48% and the LIC share would be 30.24%, leaving a residual shareholding of 15% with the GoI and 19% with the LIC.
The decision of the CCEA was implemented through a two-stage, competitive bidding process supported by a multi-layered, collective decision-making mechanism consisting of the Inter-Ministerial Group (IMG), the Core Group of Secretaries on Disinvestment (CGD) and the Alternative Mechanism (AM) consisting of an empowered Group of Cabinet Ministers.
The Preliminary Information Memorandum (PIM) inviting Expression of Interest (EoI) from all interested parties was issued on 07.10.2022. Only the parties found ‘Fit and Proper’ by the RBI and granted security clearance by the MHA could participate in the bidding stage, for which a Request for Proposal was issued for inviting technical and financial bids from the Qualified Interested Parties (QIPs). Of the five parties who initially submitted their expression of interest, four parties qualified as per the eligibility criteria and disqualification conditions prescribed therein, of which, two finally submitted their techno-financial bids and became Qualified Bidders (QBs) for this Transaction.
After comprehensive evaluation by the CGD and after considering the recommendations of the Alternative Mechanism, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) in its meeting held on 14/10/2026 approved M/s 10955230 Canada Inc. (parent entity M/s Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd.) as the Strategic Buyer for this Transaction for a purchase consideration of Rs.52,878.0806181 Crores (in words Rupees Fifty-Two Thousand Eight Hundred Seventy-Eight Crore Eight Lakh Six Thousand and One Hundred Eighty-One only) for the acquisition of 60.72% stake in the IDBI Bank Ltd, comprising 30.48% equity shareholding held by the Gol and 30.24% equity shareholding held by the LIC.
In such transactions, there is no
a-priori
benchmark for bidding. The bidders do their own valuation and submit their bids in sealed envelopes in a confidential manner. Independent agencies are hired to do a fair valuation of the enterprise contemporaneously, which is then used as a comparator to assess the reasonableness of the bids submitted.
Under this transaction, the initial bids were invited in the financial year 2025-26. For comparison, a reserve price of Rs.94.42 per share was fixed at that time, which was directly and indirectly influenced by the impacted market price. The unimpacted counter-factual was not visible at that time, except that the unimpacted pre-EoI price of the IDBI stock was Rs.42.40 per share on the last trading day before the issue of the PIM/EoI on 07.10.2022. In contrast, the impacted price was Rs.108.12 per share on the last trading day before the invitation of initial bids on 08.01.2026. The initial bids fell short of the reserve price arrived at that time and were not approved. When it became known that the initial bids have not succeeded, the impacted stock market price itself corrected, and fell significantly below the discovered bid price of Rs.75 per share.
Subsequently, in exercise of the powers delegated and conferred upon the collective decision-making mechanism, and to enhance the value of the transaction as far as possible, sealed bids reflecting their best offers were invited from the qualified bidders in the financial year 2026-27. The stock price of the IDBI Stock was Rs.70.38 per share on the trading day last before the invitation of best offer bids on 18.05.2026.
The stock market price of the narrowly traded IDBI stock continued to be volatile and fluctuated both above and below the bid discovered price with a high-low range of Rs.118.38 to Rs.61.01 per share over the valuation period. The stock market price was consequently disregarded, as it tended to misalign valuation with the intrinsic value of the enterprise. Instead, Relative Valuation by the Market Multiple Method, which overcomes this problem, was used to determine the fair market value of the enterprise on the basis of 31st March, 2026 closing accounts of all public sector banks. Additionally, the Asset Valuation Method, which considers both tangible and intangible assets, including land and properties along with the liabilities, was used to determine the fair net asset value of the enterprise as per the 31st March, 2026 audited accounts of the IDBI Bank Ltd.
Accordingly, the fair valuation of the enterprise was carried out by two professional valuation agencies using two independent methodologies as explained above. The average of these fair valuations was Rs.75.99 per share, which served as the benchmark price for the evaluation of the qualified bids. Since the winning best offer bid of Rs.81 per share was above the benchmark price, as well as fair value estimates of both the independent valuation agencies, it was adjudged to be reasonable and approved.
The successful bidder will be required to present its credentials to the Reserve Bank of India in accordance with the Fit and Proper Assessment conducted at the EoI stage and submit its roadmap for the compliance of regulatory conditions prescribed therein. Once completed, this will be the largest FDI in the financial sector of our economy so far.
The CCEA has also delegated powers to the Alternative Mechanism to undertake minority stake sales of the GoI residual shareholding (15% of the total shareholding of the IDBI Bank Ltd.) through the open market in accordance with the standard operating procedure. The LIC will be free to manage its residual shareholding in accordance with its internal procedures while ensuring compliance with the directions of its regulators.

title: NCISM Chairperson launches CCRAS SPARK 5.0 and CCRAS Ayurshodh 2026 to strengthen Ayurveda research and innovation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 8:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Chairperson of National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM), Prof. Maneesha Kothekar, today launched CCRAS SPARK 5.0 and CCRAS Ayurshodh 2026 (2nd circular) of the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS). The initiatives aim to strengthen the research ecosystem in Ayurveda by encouraging research among undergraduate students and recognising scholarly excellence, research communication and innovation.
CCRAS SPARK 5.0
The Studentship Program for Ayurveda Research Ken (SPARK) 5.0 for 2026-27 is the fifth edition of the programme. It seeks to introduce undergraduate Ayurveda students to research methodology and techniques through short-term independent research projects, and to foster research aptitude, analytical thinking and early interest in research as a career among BAMS students.
A total of 300 studentships are being offered, with a studentship amount of ₹50,000.
BAMS students in their third/fourth/professional years studying in NCISM/Government of India-recognised colleges or universities are eligible.
Registration opens on 15 October 2026. The last date for submission of applications is 15 November 2026.
CCRAS Ayurshodh – National Research Recognitions
CCRAS Ayurshodh provides a platform to recognise and encourage research contributions in Ayurveda across three categories:
CCRAS-Prabodh 3MT: Communication of research through three-minute thesis presentations.
CCRAS-Prakash: Recognition of scholarly achievements through publications based on original research.
CCRAS-Navonmesha: Recognition of innovative prototypes, novel solutions, process innovations and transformative research methodologies.
The second circular details the awards, including prize money sponsored by Shree Dhootapapeshwar Limited. The finals of CCRAS Ayurshodh are scheduled for 11 December 2026.
Prof. (Vaidya) Rabinarayan Acharya, Director General, CCRAS; Dr. Ranjit Puranik, MD and CEO, Shree Dhootapapeshwar Limited; Presidents of various NCISM boards and heads of CCRAS institutes across the country were present on the occasion.
The initiatives are intended to nurture emerging research talent, promote effective research communication, encourage quality scholarly publications and foster innovative approaches to advancing Ayurveda research.

title: ITRA, Jamnagar to Organise National Symposium ‘Ayutech Navonmesh 2026’ on Artificial Intelligence in Ayurveda
subtitle: Two-day event on October 15–16 to explore the integration of traditional Ayurvedic knowledge with modern digital technologies on the occasion of the Institute’s Sixth Foundation Day
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, under the Ministry of Ayush, will organise the Dr. P. M. Mehta Oration and the two-day national symposium ‘Ayutech Navonmesh 2026’ on October 15 and 16, 2026, to mark the Institute’s Sixth Foundation Day. The central theme of the symposium is ‘Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Ayurveda’. The event aims to explore opportunities for advancing research, innovation and healthcare services through the integration of traditional Ayurvedic knowledge with modern digital technologies.
The programme will be held under the leadership of Prof. (Dr.) Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA. Hon’ble Member of Parliament Smt. Poonamben Madam will attend as the Chief Guest. Mr. Sameer Pujari, Head of Data, Digital Health, Analytics and Artificial Intelligence in the Division of Health Systems at the World Health Organization (WHO), Switzerland, and Dr. Shyama Kuruvilla, Director of the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre, will also participate in the event. Distinguished guests will include Prof. Shailendra Saraf, Director, National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER), Gandhinagar; Dr. Mansi Deshpande, Vice-Chancellor, Gujarat Ayurved University; and Dr. Manoj Nesari, former Adviser (Ayurveda), Ministry of Ayush.
The participation of these eminent experts is expected to facilitate meaningful deliberations on the convergence of Ayurveda and modern digital technologies, with a focus on research and innovation. National and international experts will discuss the potential applications of artificial intelligence and digital technologies in Ayurvedic research, drug development, education and healthcare delivery.
The symposium will feature expert lectures, academic discussions, deliberations on research and technological collaboration, institutional recognitions and cultural programmes. Special emphasis will be placed on the ethical, scientific and practical applications of AI in Ayurvedic research, drug development, quality assurance, medical education and healthcare services.
Prof. (Dr.) Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA, said that the integration of Ayurveda and artificial intelligence could open up new avenues for research and innovation. She emphasised that connecting traditional knowledge with modern scientific and data-driven approaches could contribute meaningfully to the advancement of Ayurveda, knowledge exchange and the strengthening of public healthcare services.
Through this initiative, ITRA, Jamnagar, aims to provide a common platform for Ayurveda scholars, researchers, practitioners and technology experts, while promoting responsible technological innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration in traditional medicine.
About ITRA, Jamnagar
Dedicated to the nation by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on October 15, 2020, ITRA is the first institution in the country to receive the status of an Institution of National Importance in the field of Ayurveda. Located in Jamnagar, a city renowned for its historical and academic traditions in Ayurveda, the Institute promotes education and research through programmes ranging from undergraduate to doctoral levels, along with courses related to Ayurveda pharmacy, yoga and naturopathy.
The Institute operates a 300-bed hospital accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH), where an average of approximately 1,000 patients receive treatment daily through the Outpatient Department (OPD). Since its establishment, the Institute has provided consultation and treatment to a total of 18,47,807 patients through its OPD, while 27,520 patients have received inpatient care. Currently, 20 OPDs are functioning across various departments of the Institute. In addition, weekly OPD services are provided at eight locations across Jamnagar city and district.
The Institute also houses six laboratories accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), equipped with modern scientific instruments, along with dedicated facilities for yoga and naturopathy.
In the fields of education and research, ITRA has signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with 27 institutions, including 18 national and nine international institutions. Its Ayurveda library houses more than 30,000 books and over 5,000 manuscripts. The Institute also maintains an animal house facility for medical and pharmaceutical research in accordance with prescribed standards.

title: KAUMARACON 2026 to Begin at AIIA, New Delhi, on October 15; Vice-President to Address International Ayurveda Paediatrics Conference
subtitle:
Three-Day Conference from October 15–17 to Bring Together National and International Experts in Child Healthcare

AIIA to Celebrate Foundation Day on October 17
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 8:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, will organise KAUMARACON 2026, the International Conference on Kaumarabhritya (Ayurveda Paediatrics), from October 15 to 17, 2026, at its Sarita Vihar campus in New Delhi.
The three-day conference will bring together experts, academicians, researchers, practitioners and students from India and abroad to deliberate on advancements in Ayurveda-based child healthcare, research and clinical practice.
The inaugural session on October 15 will be attended by the Hon’ble Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, as the Chief Guest. Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, and Minister of State, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, will attend as the Guest of Honour. Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, and Dr. Maneesha Upendra Kothekar, Chairperson, National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM), will also be present.
Highlighting the Institute’s journey and achievements, Prof. (Vaidya) P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, said that the Institute, conceptualised in 2002 and dedicated to the nation by the Hon’ble Prime Minister in 2017, is entering its tenth year. He noted that AIIA has made significant progress in Ayurveda education, patient care and research. AIIA, New Delhi, has more than 200 inpatient beds and advanced diagnostic facilities, while the establishment of AIIA Goa in 2022 has further expanded its institutional reach. He added that KAUMARACON 2026 reflects the Institute’s commitment to advancing specialised Ayurveda healthcare, particularly in the field of child health.
AIIA is affiliated with the University of Delhi for postgraduate education and PhD research programmes and has received NAAC A++ accreditation. Its hospital is accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH). The Institute undertakes academic, intramural, extramural and industry-sponsored research projects and publishes three research journals.
Kaumarabhritya: Advancing Comprehensive Child Healthcare
Kaumarabhritya is a specialised branch of Ayurveda that focuses on child health and well-being, including growth and development, nutrition, immunity, mental health and the management of childhood diseases.
The Department of Kaumarabhritya at AIIA provides outpatient and inpatient services, newborn care through a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), vaccination, mental healthcare and skin care. The department also operates a specialised outpatient service for cancer care in children and attends to approximately 120–150 children daily in its outpatient section.
The department has established the KINDER Lab (Kaumarabhritya Initiative for Neurology, Dermatology, Respiratory and related areas), a specialised diagnostic facility supporting clinical assessment and research in paediatric healthcare.
Prof. Dr. Rajagopala S., Head of the Department of Kaumarabhritya, AIIA, and Organising Chairman of KAUMARACON 2026, said that children’s health and well-being are fundamental to building a healthy society. He emphasised that Kaumarabhritya addresses the comprehensive healthcare needs of children, from nutrition and immunity to physical growth, mental well-being and disease management. He added that the conference would facilitate scientific exchange, dissemination of research findings and collaboration among professionals working in Ayurveda paediatrics.
The third edition of KAUMARACON follows the conferences held in 2019 and 2023 at Ayurveda University, Jodhpur, Rajasthan. The 2026 edition is expected to attract more than 500 participants, including experts, teachers, practitioners, postgraduate scholars and students from across the country. International experts from Brazil, the United States, Germany, Sri Lanka and Nepal are also expected to participate online.
The scientific programme will include a pre-conference workshop on computer-aided drug designing (Ayurinformatics) and diagnostics in paediatrics, an oration lecture, six scientific sessions, including a session with international experts, and 12 parallel sessions.
More than 175 scientific papers are scheduled to be presented during the conference. The deliberations will provide a platform for sharing research outcomes, clinical experiences and innovative approaches in Ayurveda paediatrics. The conference aims to promote evidence-based scientific dialogue, encourage interdisciplinary collaboration and strengthen the role of Ayurveda in comprehensive child healthcare.
The three-day programme will culminate on October 17 with the Foundation Day celebrations of the All India Institute of Ayurveda, commemorating the Institute’s establishment, institutional growth and contributions to Ayurveda education, healthcare and research.
The Foundation Day programme will highlight the Institute’s achievements in academic excellence, patient care, research and the development of specialised healthcare services. Faculty members, students, researchers, practitioners and invited guests are expected to participate in the celebrations.
Through KAUMARACON 2026 and its Foundation Day celebrations, AIIA seeks to promote specialised paediatric healthcare, strengthen scientific research and foster knowledge exchange, while advancing Ayurveda’s contribution to the country’s healthcare system.

title: Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 to Be Celebrated at the National Level  Tomorrow by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, is organising the national-level celebration of Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 on 15 October 2026 at the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. The programme aims to recognise and honour the significant contributions of women farmers to Indian agriculture and highlight their role in advancing agricultural development and building a Viksit Bharat. The day also coincides with the International Day of Rural Women, established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2007, highlighting the contribution of rural women to agricultural and rural development.
Women are an integral part of India's agricultural system. From sowing, transplanting and harvesting to livestock management, seed conservation, natural resource management and value addition, women contribute significantly across the agricultural value chain. Their traditional knowledge, role in biodiversity conservation, entrepreneurial initiatives and adoption of sustainable agricultural practices are vital to strengthening rural livelihoods and enhancing agricultural resilience. As per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, females constituted 59.8% of the total workforce engaged in agricultural activities during January–December 2025.
The year 2026 has been declared the International Year of the Woman Farmer (IYWF 2026) by the United Nations, providing an important global platform to recognise the contributions of women farmers to agrifood systems and promote their empowerment. The observance further underscores the need to enhance opportunities for women in agriculture and strengthen their access to resources, technology and institutional support.
The theme for Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 is “Role of Women Farmers in Building Developed Agriculture and a Developed India.” The theme highlights the leadership of women in achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat through the adoption of modern agricultural technologies, crop diversification, livestock management, and conservation of natural resources and the development of agriculture-based enterprises. Women farmers are contributing to making agriculture more productive, sustainable and self-reliant.
The programme will bring together outstanding women farmers from various States and Union Territories, along with women agricultural officers, agricultural extension functionaries and officers and officials of DA&FW. It will provide a platform to recognise their achievements, facilitate the sharing of experiences and successful practices and encourage greater participation and leadership of women across the agricultural sector.
This year Mahila Kisan  is also being celebrated across States/UTs, Extension Education Institutes (EEIs), SAMETIs and MANAGE. Each venue is having participation of elected representatives, officials, scientists, extension workers, and other stakeholders, alongside 50-100 women farmers. Particular emphasis has been given on securing the participation of women farmers from tribal regions.
Women agricultural officers and extension functionaries also play a crucial role in connecting agricultural research with farming communities. Through the dissemination of scientific farming practices, promotion of modern technologies, training and awareness generation about government schemes, they help farmers access knowledge and improve agricultural practices.
The celebration of Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 reaffirms the importance of women's empowerment in achieving agricultural progress and rural prosperity. Recognising women farmers, ensuring equal opportunities and strengthening their access to modern technology and essential resources are important steps
towards building developed agriculture and a developed India.

title: Union Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan participates in the 10th National Convention of Agrivision in Delhi
subtitle:
“Fake agricultural colleges will be brought under control; Agriculture Council to be established soon”: Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh

“Agricultural students’ degrees will not be allowed to go to waste; government to work on short-term and long-term roadmaps”: Shri Shivraj Singh

“You deliberate and bring forth the nectar of ideas; we will implement them”: Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan announces at the Agrivision convention

“Foodgrain production has increased by 49 per cent in 10 years; India has become the world’s largest rice producer”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

“Along with further improving farmers’ livelihoods, India will no longer merely feed itself but will emerge as the world’s food basket”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 6:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan addressed the 10th National Convention of Agrivision at Pusa, Delhi, today. He said that, while further improving farmers’ livelihoods, India would no longer remain limited to meeting its own food requirements but would emerge as the ‘food basket’ of the entire world in the coming years. He made it clear that strict measures would be taken to curb the proliferation of private agricultural colleges operating without proper standards and issuing fake degrees. An Agriculture Council would soon be established to regulate these institutions and bring greater accountability to agricultural education. The government’s focus would be on ensuring quality in agricultural education, safeguarding students’ futures and strengthening the contribution of agriculture to the country’s development.
From an era of scarcity to self-reliance and record production
In his address, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan highlighted the journey of Indian agriculture, recalling a time when the country had to depend on imported foodgrains under the PL-480 programme. Today, however, through the hard work of Indian farmers and the adoption of modern policies, the country has achieved complete self-reliance in foodgrain production. Between 2014 and 2024, India’s total agricultural production increased by 49 per cent. The country now ranks first in the world in rice production and exports, while it ranks second in wheat production. He emphasised that the challenge before India was no longer simply to increase production. Instead, the focus must shift towards scientific storage, efficient management and expanding exports to global markets. Strengthening these areas would help ensure that the country makes the best possible use of its agricultural output while creating further opportunities for farmers.
“You bring forth the nectar of ideas; we will formulate policies and implement them”
Shri Shivraj Chouhan described the expertise of students and farmers’ organisations as particularly important in the policymaking process. Calling upon the experts and students attending the convention to contribute their ideas and insights, the Union Minister said, “Deliberate in depth at this national convention and bring forth the nectar in the form of your conclusions. The government will take responsibility for sharing these ideas in the national interest and implementing them.” He emphasised that the discussions should lead to practical recommendations capable of contributing to agricultural development and addressing the challenges faced by farmers and students. Announcing a follow-up meeting, he said he would meet the representatives again within the next 15 days to one month to develop a detailed action plan based on the convention’s conclusions. The follow-up discussions would focus directly on developing and implementing both short-term and long-term plans, ensuring that the recommendations emerging from the convention translated into concrete action.
Safeguarding the future of agricultural students is the top priority
Emphasising the need to raise the standard of agricultural education, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Chouhan said that no institution would be permitted to operate merely as a business that collected fees and distributed degrees without maintaining appropriate standards. The government would ensure that technical qualifications pursued by young people, including Bachelor of Science in Agriculture (BSc Agriculture) and Master of Science in Agriculture (MSc Agriculture), retained their value and were not rendered useless. He stressed the importance of protecting students’ investments of time, effort and money in their education by ensuring that agricultural institutions provided meaningful and credible qualifications. The proposed regulatory measures would seek to prevent the proliferation of substandard colleges and fake degrees while helping maintain the quality and credibility of agricultural education. The objective is to ensure that students receive an education that supports their future prospects and enables them to contribute effectively to the agricultural sector.
An ‘integrated farming’ model for small farmers
Referring to India’s average landholding size of just 0.96 hectares, Shri Chouhan said that diversification was essential to increase the incomes of small and marginal farmers. Their livelihoods could be made more secure and prosperous by integrating multiple agricultural activities rather than depending solely on grain cultivation. Alongside foodgrain production, farmers should be encouraged to take up fruit and vegetable cultivation, medicinal plant farming, animal husbandry, fisheries, beekeeping and natural farming. Integrating these activities would help diversify income sources, reduce dependence on a single crop and strengthen the economic security of farming households. He also highlighted the need to accelerate the adoption of modern technologies in agriculture. Efforts were being stepped up to integrate artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and robotics into farming, helping modernise agricultural practices and improve their efficiency. Combining diversified farming systems with technological advancements would support efforts to enhance productivity and improve farmers’ livelihoods.
During the programme, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan released a special booklet documenting Agrivision’s 10-year journey. A large number of agricultural scientists, researchers and students from across the country attended the national convention. Their participation provided an opportunity for experts and young people associated with agriculture to engage in discussions on the sector’s challenges, future priorities and development opportunities.

Agri-Tech, Food Systems and Nutrition

ICAR in ESTIC 2026

ICAR is directly associated with the thematic session on “Agri-Tech, Food Systems and Nutrition,” one of the 12 major thematic sessions of ESTIC-2026, scheduled for 29th October 2026. The session will be chaired by the Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, and the Secretary, Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI). It will feature a keynote address, presentations by a deep-tech startup CEO, a woman entrepreneur and science and technology (S&T) leaders, followed by a panel discussion. The session will provide a platform to highlight the contribution of agricultural research, innovation and emerging technologies to India's broader science and technology landscape. Several ICAR scientists, including researchers from ICAR–Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), ICAR–National Institute for Plant Biotechnology and ICAR–National Rice Research Institute, are also listed among the speakers at ESTIC-2026. ICAR's participation will highlight advances in artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, digital agriculture, advanced crop improvement, gene editing and sustainable agricultural systems. In addition, ICAR will showcase its innovations under the theme “Agri-Tech, Food Systems and Nutrition” at the ESTIC-2026 exhibition.
ESTIC-2026

Organised by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), Ministry of Science and Technology, under the guidance of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser, Government of India, with the National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology (NIIST) as the Organising Partner, the three-day event will provide a platform for showcasing cutting-edge research, emerging technologies and deep-tech innovations and fostering collaboration in emerging and critical areas of science, technology and innovation towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

content:
Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL), under its CSR initiative has signed MoUs with the District Administration of Sundargarh on tuesday for five developmental projects worth ₹22.64 crore. The projects include the rejuvenation and beautification of Kata Bandha (₹4.32 crore), Brahamani Bandha (₹3.98 crore) and Abdul Hussain Bandha (₹2.69 crore); freshwater inland aquaculture in mining-affected areas of Hemgir Block (₹3.81 crore); and renovation, improvement and construction of tanks under Talsara Assembly Constituency (₹7.84 crore) in Sundargarh district.

The aquaculture project will be implemented in-line with the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana which will benefit over 700 small-scale farmers and FPO members through the development of 50 new ponds and renovation of 20 existing ponds. Besides this, it also includes formation of women-led fish seed production units and Custom Hiring Centres, an Aqua Business School and a Fish Farmers Producers' Organisation (FFPO).
Through these initiatives, MCL aims to strengthen water resource management, promote sustainable livelihoods, support women-led enterprises and contribute to the socio-economic development of communities across Sundargarh district of Odisha.

subtitle: Discussions Focus on Expanding Bilateral Trade, Improving Market Access and Facilitating Business-to-Business Exchanges
date:

                14 OCT 2026 8:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The third meeting of the India–Brunei Darussalam Joint Trade Committee (JTC) was convened to review bilateral trade and economic cooperation and identify avenues for strengthening commercial ties between the two countries. The meeting was co-chaired by Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, India, Shri Amit Verma, and Permanent Secretary (Economy & Trade), Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Brunei Darussalam, Dr. May Fa'ezah Ahmad Ariffin. Representatives from relevant Ministries, Departments and organisations of both countries participated in the deliberations.
The discussions focused on expanding bilateral trade, addressing market access priorities and identifying institutional mechanisms to facilitate business-to-business exchanges. Both sides also deliberated on facilitating exports of agricultural and animal products from India to Brunei Darussalam, with a view to supporting food security and diversifying trade.
Pharmaceuticals, healthcare and energy were identified as key areas for further cooperation. Both sides explored opportunities for regulatory collaboration, procurement and healthcare services, recognising the potential for greater engagement in the pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors. Discussions on energy covered traditional and emerging energy partnerships to support sustained industrial growth.
The two sides also emphasised the importance of strengthening people-to-people ties and commercial outreach through cooperation in tourism and participation in trade fairs and exhibitions. They noted that targeted trade promotion events and reciprocal business delegations could help identify investment opportunities in manufacturing, infrastructure and services.
Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining regular communication between relevant nodal agencies and working groups to monitor follow-up actions and advance the trade and investment objectives discussed during the meeting.
The next meeting of the India–Brunei Darussalam Joint Trade Committee will be held in Brunei Darussalam.

title: Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC) Celebrates World Standards Day 2026 at TEC New Delhi, Highlighting India's Pivotal Role in Global Telecommunication Standardization
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC), the National Standardization Body in the telecommunications sector under the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, celebrated World Standards Day 2026 today at Manak Hall, TEC, New Delhi reaffirming India's commitment to strengthening its role in global technology development and standardization.
The momentous event was attended by all senior officers of TEC. The celebration highlighted TEC's instrumental role in formulating telecommunications standards, driving domestic technological self-reliance, and actively contributing to international standardization bodies such as the International Telecommunication Union's Standardization Sector (ITU-T).
Milestone Achieved in Standardization
Under the Telecommunications (Framework to Notify Standards, Conformity Assessment and Certification) Rules, 2025, TEC formulates standards, recognizes Conformity Assessment Bodies (CAB) and issues certificates. TEC has released 596 standards in different technology domains including Essential requirements, Generic Requirements, Test Guides and Standard Documents of TEC. TEC has designated 82 CABs till date and further more than 5400 certificates have been issued.
TEC’s Leadership and Contribution to Global Standardization
Functioning under the Ministry of Communications, TEC serves as the national body for developing standards for telecommunication equipment, services, and networks in India. During the event, the Senior DDG & Head of TEC, Shri Syed Tausif Abbas commended the relentless efforts of TEC officers for representing India globally by holding pivotal leadership roles across various ITU-T Study Groups.
The address further highlighted that robust national standards formulated by TEC not only safeguard consumer interests and ensure network security, interoperability, and quality of service (QoS), but also successfully align India's digital ecosystem with global benchmarks.

title: Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to honor top-performing States/UTs, District Police and Police Stations for recovery of lost mobile handsets through Sanchar Saathi
subtitle:
Awards to be presented in upcoming National, Zonal & State level Events of DoT

Number of handsets traceable and recovered are to be key performance parameters
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India will recognize and award the best-performing States/Union Territories (UTs), Police Districts and Police Stations for their exemplary efforts in recovering lost/stolen mobile handsets traced through the Sanchar Saathi portal - a citizen centric initiative of DoT to empower mobile subscribers, strengthen their security and increase awareness about citizen centric initiatives of the Government. The awards will be presented during the upcoming National, Zonal & State level Events of DoT.
The initiative aims to acknowledge the significant contribution of State/UT Police authorities in tracing and recovering lost or stolen mobile handsets and returning them to their rightful owners. It also seeks to encourage greater coordination between DoT, its License Service Area (LSA) field units, police authorities and telecom operators, promote the adoption of effective recovery practices, and improve recovery outcomes for citizens across the country.
The awards will be based on measurable performance parameters, i.e based on accuracy (i.e handsets recovered against trace generated) and total
number of handsets recovered etc. These parameters will help recognize the scale, accuracy and timeliness of recovery efforts undertaken by States/UTs, Police Districts and Police Stations. The detailed evaluation methodology and applicable assessment period will be finalized by DoT.
The State/UT-wise data on mobile handsets traced and recovered through the Sanchar Saathi portal is publicly available on the portal’s dashboard, which also provides visibility into recovery trends. This data will serve as an important reference for assessing performance and identifying high-performing jurisdictions and police units.
Sanchar Saathi portal facilitates the blocking and tracing of lost or stolen mobile handsets through the Central Equipment Identity Register (CEIR) facility. When a reported handset is subsequently detected on a telecom network, traceability information is generated and made available to the respective Police authorities, supporting police efforts to locate and recover the device. An alert regarding the traceability is also sent to the citizen through SMS and email.
The initiative reflects the importance of close coordination among DoT, its LSA field units, Telecom Service Providers and State/UT Police authorities in strengthening mobile security and protecting citizens’ digital assets. The proposed awards will provide a platform to recognize outstanding work, encourage healthy performance-driven competition and promote the sharing of successful practices across jurisdictions.
DoT reiterates its commitment to strengthening the Sanchar Saathi ecosystem and supporting law-enforcement agencies in improving the recovery of lost and stolen mobile handsets. Citizens can access the portal at www.sancharsaathi.gov.in or use Sanchar Saathi Mobile app to report lost or stolen mobile handsets and avail following citizen centric services.
Services at the fingertips of every citizen
Sanchar Saathi brings the following citizen-centric services on a single platform:
Chakshu
– Report suspected fraud communication and spam: Report suspicious calls, SMS or WhatsApp messages – such as fake KYC or bill- payment alerts, impersonation of Government, police or bank officials, and fraudulent investment, job or loan offers – in a few simple steps.
Know mobile connections in your name:
Check all mobile connections issued on your identity and report those which you have not taken or no longer require, so that they cannot be misused.
Block your lost or stolen mobile handset:
Block the handset across the networks of all telecom operators so that it cannot be used anywhere in India, enable its tracing, and unblock it once it is found.
Know the genuineness of your mobile handset:
Verify a handset through its IMEI number before buying a new or second-hand phone.
Report incoming international calls with Indian numbers:
Report calls from abroad that are disguised as domestic (+91) numbers, helping the Government act against illegal telecom set-ups.
Trusted Contact Details:
Verify the genuine customer care numbers, email IDs and website links of banks and financial institutions before sharing any information.
Keep Yourself Aware:
Access awareness material on prevailing fraud trends such as fake loan apps, investment scams, fake job calls and fake traffic challans
DoT is fully committed to ensure safety of citizens through its proactive actions for curbing misuse of telecom resources for cybercrime and financial frauds. Sanchar Saathi is also available as mobile app and can be downloaded from:

title: DoT and ITU organise AI for Good Build-a-thon 5.0 at India Mobile Congress 2026
subtitle:
Dr. Bilel Jamoussi, Deputy Director and Chief, Study Groups and Policy Department, Telecommunication Standardization Bureau, ITU inaugurates the Build-a-thon 5.0 in the august presence of senior DoT leadership and distinguished experts

Build-a-thon 5.0 focuses on building Agentic AI solutions complied with Indian policies in the domain of telecommunications
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, in collaboration with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), organised the Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Good Build-a-thon 5.0, a hands-on capacity-building event that brought together teams from across the country to develop Agentic AI solutions for the telecommunications sector on the last day of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi.
The event, themed “
Creating innovative agents in 5G
”, was inaugurated by Dr. Bilel Jamoussi, Deputy Director and Chief, Study Groups and Policy Department, Telecommunication Standardization Bureau, ITU, in the august presence of senior DoT leadership and distinguished representatives from academia, industry, international organisations and the technology ecosystem.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Jamoussi underscored the importance of Agentic AI solutions that are contextualized to the country, compliant with international standards and governed by local policies. He stressed that, to fully realize the benefits of integrating AI into workflows, policy gaps must be identified through real AI solutions and then addressed in regulation.
Strong leadership from Shri Prabhat Dikshit, DDG(Satellite) and Shri Bishnu Dubey, Director (AS-II), DoT along with support from C-DoT and the organizing teams was critical for the success of this event. The judges panel also included Shri Amit Shrivastava, DDG(MT), TEC, Dr. Brajesh Mishra, Executive Director, C-DoT and Shri Prachish Khanna, DDG(Media), DoT.
From Kick-off to Prototypes
The Build-a-thon 5.0 opened in early July with more than 25 registered teams, each with an average of four members. During the preparation phase, ITU and DoT experts held five online mentoring sessions covering the Build-a-thon problem statements, the ITU-T Y.3172 standardized machine learning pipeline, the ITU AI Readiness 2.0 report (a global benchmark for AI Ready use cases) and open-source data sources.
More than 10 hours of mentoring resulted in 16 well-designed AI prototype submissions. The entries featured a range of agent types, including knowledge-base agents that solve domain-specific problems, policy and legal adviser agents that play an institutional role within the solution, and coordinator agents that orchestrate multiple agents.
Standout Solutions
Several submissions distinguished themselves:
Multi-agent network analysis with policy mapping:
One solution combines a country-specific 5G/telecom knowledge base with multi-agent AI analysis, progressive network-error scenarios, policy and standards mapping, gap identification, human supervision and auditable evidence.
Unified traffic and security controller:
Another proposes an AI agent-based controller that manages traffic priority and security together, based on three inputs: service intent, available network resources and data sensitivity.
Law inside the control loop:
A third embeds regulation directly into network operations. Three optimizer agents (Spectrum, Energy and Slicing) propose actions, while a Regulator agent with veto power checks each against ten rules grounded in Indian telecom law, citing the official text. A Policy & Legal Adviser answers questions drawn from 16 official documents, and a gap analyzer reports where Indian law is silent.
Judges noted the energy and dedication of the participating teams, and lively discussions took place between judges and teams during the interaction session. Presentations clearly set out each use case’s problem statement and its mapping against policy, standards and global benchmarks, and were accompanied by live demonstrations showing concrete evidence, including error scenarios and policy gaps.
The engaging session wrapped up with an exciting prize distribution by ITU and DoT dignitaries.
The 1st prize went to Team Netaxis, RVCE Bangalore, for “
Context Aware Agentic Orchestration of QoS and Adaptive Security in Resource Constrained 5G”.
The 2nd prize was presented to Team SNR, for “
knowledge-grounded retrieval, deterministic constraint validation and multi-agent arbitration”.
The 3rd prize went to team Agentnet for “
TeleAgent: Collaborative Multi Agent Framework Using a Fine Tuned Small Language model for Automated Private 5G Network Troubleshooting”.
A special women’s prize was awarded to team Orbitflow (SNU Chennai) & team Handshake protocol for “
Predictive Traffic-aware Beam Hopping for LEO Non-Terrestrial Networks” and “Law-aware AI agents for 5G emergency response”.
Lastly, the judges’ prize was presented to team Nethealers for “
Autonomous Self-Healing 5G Radio Access Network Agent with Foundation-Model Diagnosis and Digital-Twin Pre-Validation”.
Build-a-thon 5.0 demonstrates India’s strong potential to lead in AI solutions for the telecommunications domain and in the policy design that governs them.

title: Quality Infrastructure, Clean Energy and Consumer Safety Take Centre Stage at the National Celebration of World Standards Day 2026
subtitle:
Union Cabinet Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi Highlights Role of Standards in India’s Clean Energy Transition

MoS Shri B. L. Verma and Smt. Nimuben J Bambhaniya Address BIS World Standards Day Event in Delhi

BIS Launches Silver Refinery Scheme and Roadmap for Sustainable Agriculture and Sustainable Manufacturing 

New Indian Standards Released for the Emerging Technology, Clean Energy, Traditional Medicine & Healthcare
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a major push toward strengthening national quality infrastructure and accelerating India’s clean energy transition, Bureau of Indian Standards unveiled BIS Silver Refinery Scheme, New Indian Standards on emerging technologies & clean energy mobility and a standardization roadmap for sustainable agriculture and manufacturing on the occasion of World Standards Day 2026 at the national event hosted in New Delhi.
Delivering the presidential address to standardization professionals, academicians, industry representatives and senior officials; Shri Pralhad Joshi, Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, and New & Renewable Energy, and Education; emphasized India’s commitment to quality:
“Under the vision of PM Narendra Modi ji, our journey towards Viksit Bharat is driven by a single mantra: Quality, Quality, and only Quality.”
Speaking on this year’s theme,
‘Shared Vision for a Better World: SDG 7 (Clean & Affordable Energy)’
, Shri Joshi highlighted the role of Indian Standards developed by BIS in shaping India’s energy transformation.
Congratulating BIS on its ongoing efforts to expand the quality ecosystem in the country, Shri B. L. Verma, Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution and Social Justice & Empowerment, underscored the fundamental impact of standards in improving quality of life of every citizen.  Smt. Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya, Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, emphasized the consumer-centric aspect of standardization. She underscored the need to expand standard development into newer domains, ensuring a balanced ecosystem that simultaneously drives industrial growth and protects consumer welfare.
Commending the landmark achievements of BIS in the recent years, Smt. Nidhi Khare, IAS, Secretary, Department of Consumer Affairs, underscored the pivotal role of standardization in establishing uniformity, consistency, and process institutionalization across public procurement and regulation. She stressed that effective consumer protection must be preventive driven by robust testing, digital enforcement, and conformity assessments.
Welcoming the delegates, Director General of BIS, Shri Sanjay Garg, said, "Standards are vital enablers of innovation, technology development, and industrial strength." He announced that BIS is among the world's first national standardization bodies to make standards’ development and its access completely digital for all stakeholders. He also highlighted major reforms at BIS supporting Ease of Doing Business.
Launch of BIS Silver Refinery Scheme
The BIS certification scheme for silver refineries and mints, extends structured purity assurance and hallmarking to silver bullion and coins across India and establishes a national framework for silver purity modelled after the existing Gold Refinery Scheme.
Following the gazette notification of Amendment No. 1 to Indian Standard IS 2112:2025 (Silver and Silver Alloys, Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking), fine silver bullion and coins of three purity grades: 999.9, 999.5, and 999.0 parts per thousand (ppt), have been included in scope of the standard, with provision for hallmarking by BIS licensed refineries and mints.
Under the scheme, BIS will grant license to qualified silver refineries and mints after assessing their technical competence, refining processes, and testing infrastructure. Licensed facilities will be authorized to apply the official BIS hallmark to silver bullion and coins conforming to the prescribed requirements.
For assured authenticity and traceability across the precious metals supply chain, hallmarked silver bullion and coins will bear a standardized BIS mark comprising of the BIS Standard Mark accompanied by the word SILVER, purity grade (999.9, 999.5, or 999.0), the manufacturer’s identification mark and a unique serial number for batch traceability.
The standard prescribes rigorous sampling and testing protocols for refineries and mints to determine the silver content in bullion and coins. These include advance analytical methods such as Gravimetric testing (IS 2113), ICP-OES difference method (IS 16900 / ISO 15096) and Spark-OES difference methods (IS 19563 / ISO 18214).
https://youtu.be/SrF8K82bTow
Launch of BIS Digital Standard Reader –
BIS Digital Standard Reader is a web-based platform that converts XML-formatted Indian Standards into interactive SMART standards. Designed to enhance accessibility, the tool enables users to search technical content, navigate hyperlinked cross-references, access an in-built dictionary, and translate text into Indian languages. Accessible across mobile devices, tablets, and desktops, the platform also features an analytics dashboard to track usage trends and establishes an AI-ready repository for future digital services. This will make Indian Standards much user friendly and easy for adaption.
Release of New Indian Standards -
On this occasion BIS announced the rollout of 7 new Indian Standards across diverse sectors, including textiles, clean mobility, therapeutic healthcare, robotics, and building materials.
Emerging Technologies & Clean Energy Mobility -
Cables for Electric Vehicle Charging Systems (IS 19967:2026):
Defines construction, insulation, thermal management, and testing protocols for flexible charging cables (up to 1,100 V AC / 1,500 V DC) operating under demanding outdoor conditions across AC Modes 1–3 and DC Mode 4 systems
Pedal Assisted Bicycles / EPACs (IS 19891:2026):
Provides standards for design, electrical circuit safety, short-circuit/overheat protection, and anti-tampering rules for Electrically Power Assisted Cycles with continuous rated power up to 0.25 kW and speed cut-off at 25 km/h
Wearable Service Robots
– Lower Limb (IS 17192 Part-6:2026): Adopts international testing criteria (identical to ISO FDIS 18646-6:2025) using anthropomorphic test dummies to evaluate the motion, stability, and performance of lower-limb assistive and rehabilitation robotics.
Healthcare–
Paediatric Panchakarma Droni (IS 19960:2026):
assuring safety, structural stability, non-toxic coatings, and oil-resistance specifications for Paediatric Panchakarma treatment tables (Droni) for Infant (birth to 2 years) and Child (2 to 10 years)
Therapeutic Footwear Specification (IS 19956:2026):
Assuring clinical and mechanical safety criteria for footwear designed for diabetic and neuropathic patients. It covers pressure relief, internal depth, rocker geometry, moisture management, and antifungal properties to mitigate foot ulceration risks.
Industrial Materials & Building Products
Flexible Plywood Specification (IS 19952:2026):
Provides standard classifications, glue bond strength grades (moisture-resistant, BWR, and BWP), and formaldehyde emission limits for curved wood-based panels used in interior design and architecture
PVC Coated Fibreglass Insect Screen (IS 19825:2026):
Outlines requirements for mesh strength, UV degradation resistance, flame propagation resistance, and structural durability for fibreglass insect screening utilized in residential and commercial spaces.
Release of National Roadmaps for Standardization in the field of Sustainable Agriculture & Manufacturing
On this occasion, a strategic roadmap developed by Environment and Ecology Division Council of BIS to establish Indian Standards for the sustainable agricultural sector was released. The document addresses challenges including climate change, resource depletion, land degradation, post-harvest losses, and inefficient nutrient use. It spans 15 categories, covering soil management, water use, agricultural inputs, emerging technologies, climate services, and socio-economic support. Aligned with the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), the roadmap outlines standard formulation across three timelines: short-term (1 year), mid-term (2–3 years), and long-term (4–5 years).
In another roadmap released today, for Sustainable Manufacturing, low-carbon technologies, resource efficiency, circular economy practices, sustainable product design, digitalisation, sustainability reporting and supply-chain management have been identified as key areas for standardisation.
Award of Best Technical Committees for Development of Standards
On the Occasion of World Standards Day, BIS presents the Best Technical Committee Award to recognise the outstanding contributions, technical expertise, and collaborative efforts of experts in advancing the development of Indian Standards in the respective sectors. This year 16 distinguished technical committees have been conferred with this prestigious award.
Addition of 6 New Academic Institutions into Standardization Framework -
In the presence of Union Minister of State Shri B L Verma and Smt Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya, BIS onboarded
IIT Ropar, NIT Manipur, NIT Meghalaya, Assam Textiles Institute, and IIT Dharwad, and RGIPT
(Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology) as MoU partner institution with an objective to integrate Indian standards into academic curricula and transform students into standards-ready professionals. As on date BIS has 98 number of MoU partner institutions working for integration of standards in academic curricula, collaborative R&D projects for standardization as well as offering internship in BIS and industry exposure to the students.
Handbook on Good Practices for Safety in the Laboratory
BIS has published a comprehensive booklet,
‘Good Practices for Safety in Laboratory,’
drawing on key standards (including IS 4209, IS 4906, and IS 9457). The reference handbook covers hazard identification, protective equipment, contamination control, and safe waste disposal for chemical, radiochemical, and microbiological facilities.
Release of Educational Comic books –
On this occasion, two new comic books on Indian Standards for Toys and Hallmarking were released by BIS to foster awareness among children about the importance of standards, quality and consumer protection from an early age. With the addition of these titles, BIS has expanded its collection to 13 comic books, strengthening its efforts to promote consumer awareness through print and digital platforms.
On the occasion of World Standards Day 2026, global standardization bodies ISO, IEC and ITU jointly released a video message sharing how shared standards build system-trust, accelerate innovation, and support sustainable trade. As India’s national standardization body, BIS participates in over 600 technical committees across ISO and IEC to align international standard development with India’s strategic interests.

title: Government Constitutes Committee to Examine Issues Relating to Sugarcane Farmers and the Sugar Sector
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution

content:
The Government of India has
constituted a committee under the chairmanship of Prof. Ramesh Chand, former Member of NITI Aayog
, to
examine issues raised by sugarcane farmers and recommend appropriate measures for addressing their concerns
.
The constitution of the Committee follows the decisions taken during a meeting of representatives of sugarcane farmers from Karnataka and Maharashtra with the Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and the Union Minister of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.
The Committee will examine the demand for an increase in remunerative returns to sugarcane farmers, taking into account cultivation costs and other relevant factors. It will
also examine the demand for revision of the ex-mill Minimum Selling Price (MSP) of sugar in the context of sugar production costs, market realisations, and the financial viability of sugar mills.
Other key areas of examination will include existing
mechanisms for testing and reporting sugar recovery, measures to ensure transparent verification of recovery
, and prevailing sugarcane weighment practices at sugar mills, including the adequacy of calibration, inspection and verification mechanisms.
The Committee will also examine
prevailing practices, relating to deductions from the weight of mechanically harvested sugarcane
and assess the extent of actual losses, if any, arising from mechanised harvesting. It will evaluate the financial impact of the present practices on the cane price payable to farmers and may consider any other related matters deemed necessary.
The Committee will
consult all stakeholders, including farmers’ representatives, sugar mill associations, State Governments and other experts or organisations, as considered necessary
. The Committee will submit its report, containing its findings and specific recommendations, as early as possible, for consideration by the competent authority.
The Chairman of the committee, Prof. Ramesh Chand, an eminent agricultural economist and public policy expert, served as a Member of NITI Aayog from 2015 to 2026 and previously as Director of ICAR-NIAP and Member of the Fifteenth Finance Commission. He has extensive expertise in agricultural development, farmers’ issues, food security, agricultural markets and pricing policy.
The Committee comprises the Agriculture Commissioner, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; Joint Secretary (Sugar), Department of Food and Public Distribution and Joint Secretary (Legal Metrology), Department of Consumer Affairs as members.

title: Ministry of Cooperation mandates new Audit Reporting Framework for Multi-State Cooperative Societies to strengthen transparency, accountability and good governance
subtitle:
Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, Ministry of Cooperation takes another significant step towards strengthening transparency, financial discipline, accountability and good governance in Multi-State Cooperative Societies

Multi-State Co-operative Societies (Auditor’s Report) Order, 2026 (MSCARO, 2026) to introduce a uniform, structured and risk-based statutory audit reporting framework

New framework to facilitate early detection of financial stress, safeguard members’ funds and strengthen compliance with statutory and governance requirements

Standardised audit reporting to enable technology-driven regulatory supervision, automated scrutiny and risk-based monitoring through the CRCS Portal

Phased implementation mandated to provide Multi-State Cooperative Societies adequate time to strengthen their systems and processes
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of
‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’
and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, the Ministry of Cooperation continue to promote a transparent, accountable, financially sound and professionally governed cooperative sector. In furtherance of the same, Ministry of Cooperation has mandated the Multi-State Co-operative Societies (Auditor’s Report) Order, 2026 (MSCARO, 2026), aimed at strengthening transparency, accountability, financial discipline and good governance in Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS). The mandated framework marks another significant step towards building a more transparent, professionally managed and accountable cooperative ecosystem while safeguarding the interests of cooperative members.
The Multi-State Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 empowered the Central Government, under Section 73(6), to prescribe auditing and accounting standards for Multi-State Cooperative Societies. In pursuance of this provision, the Ministry of Cooperation has formulated MSCARO, 2026, based on inputs received from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) and Multi-State Cooperative Societies.
Modelled on the Companies (Auditor’s Report) Order (CARO) applicable to the corporate sector, MSCARO seeks to establish a uniform, structured and risk-based framework for statutory audit reporting in Multi-State Cooperative Societies. Under the mandated framework, auditors will be required to report on important financial, administrative, governance and statutory compliance parameters through a standardized format providing for clear Yes/No responses along with relevant remarks. This will enhance consistency in audit reporting, facilitate identification of irregularities and strengthen regulatory oversight.
A major feature of the mandated framework is the introduction of risk-based regulatory supervision, enabling the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) to identify societies exhibiting higher financial or governance risks based on audit observations. This will facilitate more focused inspections, inquiries and regulatory interventions, thereby improve the effectiveness of supervision and ensure timely corrective measures.
The mandated framework will also facilitate early identification of financial stress through systematic reporting of Non-Performing Assets (NPAs), overdue loans, liquidity positions, deposits, advances, repayment defaults and borrowings. Such disclosures will help identify emerging financial vulnerabilities and enable timely remedial action before they develop into more serious financial or operational concerns.
Another important objective of MSCARO, 2026 is to strengthen the protection of members’ funds and financial interests. The mandated audit requirements will enable independent verification of investments, utilization of funds, share capital, membership records and relevant statutory approvals. By promoting greater scrutiny of financial transactions and the deployment of cooperative resources, the framework seeks to reinforce financial integrity and members’ confidence in cooperative institutions.
To further strengthen good governance and institutional accountability, the Order provides for regular scrutiny of the composition of Boards of Directors, eligibility and disqualification of directors, conduct of Annual General Meetings and Board meetings, constitution and functioning of statutory committees, and compliance relating to related-party transactions. These provisions are intended to encourage transparent decision-making, democratic functioning and adherence to statutory requirements across Multi-State Cooperative Societies.
The MSCARO also envisages technology-enabled regulatory oversight through the integration of standardized audit information with the CRCS Portal. Such integration could facilitate automated scrutiny, regulatory dashboards, risk scoring and Artificial Intelligence-based analytics, enabling more efficient monitoring, identification of compliance gaps and evidence-based regulatory interventions.
The framework further provides for audit-level verification of cybersecurity and anti-money laundering compliance, wherever applicable. This includes examination of cybersecurity safeguards, reporting of suspicious transactions, customer identification requirements and compliance relating to the appointment of Designated Directors and Principal Officers under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). These measures are expected to strengthen institutional safeguards against financial irregularities, cyber risks and other compliance-related vulnerabilities.
Recognizing the need to provide cooperative institutions adequate time to upgrade their internal systems and processes, the Ministry has mandated phased implementation of MSCARO, 2026. The long-term objective is to extend the framework to Multi-State Cooperative Societies crossing the prescribed threshold of ₹50 crore in relevant financial parameters. The initial phase will cover larger societies crossing the ₹1,000 crore threshold, allowing smaller institutions additional time to prepare for the enhanced reporting requirements.
The MSCARO, 2026 represents an important step towards a more transparent, professionally managed and accountable cooperative ecosystem by combining standardized statutory audit reporting with risk-based supervision and technology-driven monitoring, the initiative seeks to strengthen institutional credibility, protect members’ interests and advance the vision of
‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’
.
