title: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Felicitates 62 Young Innovators at 12th NLEPC, Says School Students Are Turning Ideas into Marketable Products and Entrepreneurship
subtitle:
25 students have already taken products to market; some are earning lakhs while still in school: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Around 250 intellectual property rights generated by young innovators; Minister proposes dedicated sessions involving parents

INSPIRE-MANAK has selected over 18.27 lakh students since inception in 2009; Compendium released at the ceremony
date:

                14 OCT 2026 6:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today felicitated 62 young innovators at the 12th National Level Exhibition and Project Competition (NLEPC) under INSPIRE-MANAK, saying that school students are increasingly translating their ideas into marketable products and entrepreneurial ventures.
The Minister said 25 students had already taken their products to market, while around 250 intellectual property rights had been generated by young innovators. Some students, he said, were earning lakhs of rupees while still in school, demonstrating how scientific curiosity, commitment and access to opportunities can transform ideas into practical outcomes.
The felicitation ceremony was organised by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, in collaboration with the National Innovation Foundation–India (NIF), at New Delhi. A total of 729 students participated in the event. The ceremony was attended by Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology; Prof. Anil D. Sahasrabudhe, Chairperson, National Innovation Foundation–India; Dr. Umesh Kumar Sharma, Head, Science and Technology Capacity Building Division, DST; and Dr. Arvind C. Ranade, Director, National Innovation Foundation–India, along with senior officials, teachers, mentors and other stakeholders. The INSPIRE-MANAK 2026 Compendium was also released on the occasion.
Interacting with the young innovators, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the students were the main attraction of the programme and that their work had demonstrated the true value of INSPIRE-MANAK. Recalling his initial scepticism about the programme’s name when it was introduced, he said the achievements of the participating students had convinced him of its significance and the high standards of innovation it was fostering.
The Minister referred to several projects presented at the exhibition that addressed everyday challenges through scientific and technological solutions. These included an AI-based alcohol detection system designed to prevent a vehicle from starting when alcohol is detected, an ultrasonic washing machine that can save water, a device designed to deter stray dogs through vibrations, and assistive technology for visually impaired students. He also referred to a tracking walking stick showcased at the exhibition.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said the projects demonstrated how students from Classes VI to XII, representing different parts of the country, were identifying problems around them and developing solutions with wider applications. The achievements of students who had taken products to market and secured intellectual property rights reflected the potential to progress from school-level innovation to entrepreneurship and commercial application.
Referring to India’s expanding start-up ecosystem, the Minister said the country’s start-up numbers had grown from around 350–400 in 2014 to approximately 2.5 lakh, with nearly 60 per cent located in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. He said young people today had greater access to information and opportunities, and could achieve significant outcomes through passion, commitment and hard work.
Dr. Jitendra Singh called for stronger industry partnerships to help promising student innovators improve their products, respond to market requirements and explore commercial opportunities. He suggested facilitating business-to-business interactions for young innovators so that their ideas could receive industry feedback and potentially progress towards wider application.
The Minister said promising innovations should not remain confined to exhibitions or working models. Students with entrepreneurial potential should receive opportunities to engage with industry and develop solutions that meet practical needs. He encouraged stakeholders to explore ways of connecting young innovators with relevant enterprises and technical expertise at an early stage.
Citing the example of a policy change that removed the three-year existence requirement for deep-tech start-ups supported by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), Dr. Jitendra Singh said innovation required a willingness to support new ideas and take calculated risks. He called for greater collaboration between the Government and industry to nurture student innovators and help them develop their technologies.
The Minister also stressed the importance of mentorship in enabling students to recognise their strengths, refine their ideas and navigate the journey from an initial concept to a practical application. He proposed that a future edition of the programme include a dedicated session in which young innovators could speak directly about their work and experiences.
Dr. Jitendra Singh proposed that future editions of the programme include a dedicated session in which each participating student is accompanied by at least one parent or guardian. He said parents may sometimes be unfamiliar with the nature of a child’s innovative work and, without intending to discourage them, may inadvertently interrupt the time and effort required to pursue an idea.
The Minister emphasised that parents, teachers and mentors all have an important role in creating an environment where children feel encouraged to experiment, question established approaches and learn from failure. He also stressed the need for students to understand their own capabilities, seek appropriate guidance and remain open to learning as technology and opportunities continue to evolve.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said young innovators must continue developing their skills and adapting to new knowledge rather than becoming complacent after an achievement. He encouraged them to explore their interests, make informed choices and keep improving their ideas through experimentation and practical experience.
Speaking at the event, Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology, said the exhibition reflected the ability of young students to identify problems faced by society and consider how science could help address them. He referred to the geographical diversity of participants, from the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to Kashmir and from Mizoram to Mumbai, as well as the variety of projects covering agriculture, healthcare, environmental protection, accessibility, energy, water conservation, safety and improving everyday life for older people.
INSPIRE-MANAK, which stands for Million Minds Augmenting National Aspirations and Knowledge, is a flagship initiative of the Department of Science and Technology implemented in collaboration with the National Innovation Foundation–India, an autonomous body under DST. The programme encourages students from Classes VI to XII to develop original ideas and innovations rooted in science and societal applications.
Since its inception in 2017 a total of 18,27,580 students have been selected under INSPIRE-MANAK up to 2025–26. The Department has organised 11 National Level Exhibition and Project Competitions, at which 7,444 students exhibited their innovative projects and models.
During 2023–24 and 2024–25, 46,926 and 50,009 students, respectively, were selected under the scheme. The 12th NLEPC brought together students selected during these two financial years, providing a national platform to showcase their projects, interact with experts and receive exposure and mentorship.
Under the programme, selected students are supported in developing their ideas into models and proof-of-concept prototypes, with opportunities to improve their projects through workshops and interaction with experts and leading technical institutions. The initiative aims to nurture scientific temper, creativity and innovation from an early age and encourage students to turn observations of everyday challenges into practical solutions.
Congratulating the young innovators, Dr. Jitendra Singh encouraged them to continue questioning, experimenting and learning, and to pursue opportunities to develop their ideas further. He said that supporting young innovators from the school level would help strengthen India’s innovation ecosystem and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat.

title: TDB signs agreement with ideaForge for ₹151 crore RDI support to develop YETI heavy-lift autonomous aerial logistics vehicle
subtitle: Indigenous VTOL platform designed to transport payloads of up to 200 kg, with a targeted range of 200 km, to advance towards TRL-9
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 12:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Strengthening India's capabilities in autonomous aerial systems and next-generation logistics, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with ideaForge Technology Limited, Mumbai, Maharashtra for financial support of ₹151 crore under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.
The project, with a total project cost of ₹302 crore, focuses on the development of YETI, a heavy-lift, long-range autonomous aerial logistics vehicle, with the objective of advancing the technology from Technology Readiness Level (TRL)-4 to TRL-9. The financial support will be provided through debt financing.
Designed for demanding operating environments, YETI is an autonomous vertical take-off and landing, fixed-wing hybrid unmanned aerial vehicle (VTOL-FW UAV) intended to transport heavy payloads over long distances. Its proposed capabilities are aimed at addressing logistics requirements in areas where conventional transportation can be difficult, time-consuming or operationally constrained. The platform is designed to carry payloads of up to 200 kg, with a targeted range of up to 200 km and an operating altitude of up to 6,500 metres above mean sea level. Its weather-resistant design is intended to support operations in challenging environments, including high-altitude regions, deserts and marine conditions.
A key feature of YETI is its ability to take off and land vertically while retaining a fixed-wing configuration for longer-range operations. The vehicle is designed to operate from relatively small, unprepared landing areas measuring approximately 15 metres × 15 metres, enabling deployment in locations with limited ground infrastructure.The platform incorporates distributed and redundant propulsion and power architecture to improve fault tolerance. Its proposed capabilities also include GNSS-denied navigation, a communication link of up to 200 km, swarm operations and containerised transportation for rapid deployment. The design is intended to enable the vehicle to be transported and set up quickly, supporting logistics missions across geographically challenging locations.
The development of heavy-lift autonomous aerial platforms has growing relevance for applications requiring the movement of essential supplies across difficult terrain. By combining vertical take-off and landing with long-range flight capability and substantial payload capacity, YETI is being developed to address a distinct segment of the unmanned aviation and aerial logistics market.
The RDI-supported programme will facilitate further technology development, engineering, integration, testing and validation required to progress the platform towards TRL-9, subject to the applicable technical, safety and regulatory requirements. The project falls under the Deep Technology sector, with Intelligent Systems and Robotics as the sub-sector. It reflects the growing importance of indigenous autonomous systems that integrate aerospace engineering, propulsion, navigation, communications and intelligent control.
Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said,
“The development of advanced autonomous systems is opening new possibilities for addressing complex operational and logistical challenges. Indigenous heavy-lift aerial platforms can play an important role in improving access to remote and difficult-to-reach locations. Through the RDI Fund, TDB is supporting technology-intensive projects that require sustained investment to progress from advanced development towards deployment. The agreement with ideaForge reflects our commitment to strengthening India's capabilities in autonomous systems, robotics and next-generation aerospace technologies.”
Speaking on this development, CEO and Co-founder of ideaForge Technology Ltd., said,
“YETI represents a generational leap in what India can design, build, and operate autonomously. Our armed forces and our logistics networks face the daily reality of reaching where roads end, and weather doesn’t cooperate. YETI is our answer to that challenge, which is engineered not just to fly, but to deliver, reliably and repeatably, in the conditions that define the toughest operational environments. The government’s confidence in ideaForge through the RDI framework is a reaffirmation that Indian deeptech players are now ready to carry the weight of national capability-building.”

Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojna
(BHAVYA) is a ₹33,660 crore
initiative to develop
100 plug-and-play industrial parks
across India.
The parks will provide modern industrial infrastructure
, reliable services, and faster approvals, reducing the time needed to set up new industries. The scheme aims to
attract investment, support MSMEs, strengthen supply chains, create jobs, and drive industrial growth
across regions.
A New Phase in Manufacturing Policy
India's manufacturing sector is undergoing structural change. It now contributes about
16–17 percent of GDP
and employs
over 27 million workers.
The
National Manufacturing Mission
aims to raise this share to
25 percent by 2035.
The composition of industries is also changing, with medium- and high-technology industries accounting for
46.3% of manufacturing value addition
. This reflects a shift towards higher-value and technology-intensive manufacturing.
As industries grow, they need reliable infrastructure, efficient logistics, and predictable approvals. Global supply chains are also diversifying, making well-connected industrial locations more important.
Plug-and-play parks bring these requirements together by providing essential infrastructure and common facilities before industries begin operations. This reduces the time and cost involved in setting up new manufacturing units. To expand this approach nationwide, the
Bharat Audyogik Vikas  Yojna
(
BHAVYA) was
approved by the Cabinet in March 2026 and notified on 10 April 2026
with an outlay of
₹33,660 crore
. BHAVYA is being implemented in partnership with States and private
developers
. The scheme emphasises
increasing manufacturing capacity in the country
and ease of doing business through streamlined approvals, effective single-window systems and investor-friendly reforms. The plug-and-play industrial ecosystems will reduce entry-level barriers and help industries move from investment to production quickly.
Policy Evolution: From Pre-2020 to Plug-and-Play Ecosystems
India's approach to manufacturing growth has evolved over time. Each phase has expanded the country's capacity to support industry and create new economic opportunities.
The first phase focused on
industrial estates
and
Special Economic Zones (SEZs)
. These provided industrial land, common infrastructure, and regulatory incentives. As of February 2026, India
had 370 notified
SEZs
. These zones attracted investments worth
₹7.82 lakh crore
and generated employment for over
31.7 lakh people.
The approach then expanded from individual industrial zones to larger manufacturing hubs across the country. As of 14 October 2026,
4,164 industrial
parks
have been mapped on the
India Industrial Land Bank (IILB).
At the same time, the
National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP)
moved beyond providing industrial land. It combined manufacturing zones with utilities, logistics, and urban services, creating more integrated industrial locations.
Industrial nodes such
as Dholera Special Investment Region (Gujarat), Shendra-Bidkin Industrial Area (Maharashtra), Vikram Udyogpuri (Madhya Pradesh), and Integrated Industrial Township Greater Noida (Uttar Pradesh)
demonstrated the advantages of integrated planning.

Inside the BHAVYA Framework
BHAVYA provides financial assistance of up to
₹1 crore per acre
for developing industrial parks. The scheme covers essential
components
such as internal roads, power supply, water networks, drainage systems, common effluent treatment facilities,
value-added infrastructure
and Information & Communication Technology (ICT)-enabled administration. Underground utility corridors will enable a no-dig environment for efficient maintenance and uninterrupted industrial operations.
Parks will also feature
ready-built factory sheds, built-to-suit units, testing and certification facilities, and warehousing.
To improve worker welfare and productivity, provisions have been made for
worker
housing, healthcare facilities, skill development centres, and other
social
amenities. The scheme
supports up to 25% of approved funding to be allocated for external infrastructure such as road, rail, and last-mile logistics connectivity,
ensuring seamless integration with the wider transport network.
The scheme will be implemented over six years, from
FY2026–27 to FY 2031–32
.
In the first phase,
up to 50 industrial parks will be selected
through a challenge
mode across two selection rounds
. The remaining parks will be selected in subsequent phases, taking the total number of parks supported under BHAVYA to 100. The selection will consider project readiness, land availability, and industrial potential. Each park will span
25 to 1,000 acres depending upon
mandatory criteria of land sizes as per the Scheme guidelines
. Projects will be implemented
and managed
through dedicated
Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs),
which will oversee development, operations, investor facilitation, and long-term maintenance.
Manufacturing firms, Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), startups, and investors can access common facilities and streamlined approvals under BHAVYA.
In June 2026
, the BHAVYA Portal was launched
for the implementation and monitoring of the scheme. The portal supports project submission, appraisal and evaluation while enabling a transparent and competitive selection process.
Plug and Play Industrial Parks: Concept and Features
Trunk infrastructure
is the higher-order infrastructure development with the primary purpose of serving ‘catchment’ areas to be shared between developments, commonly provided by local governments. It includes the development of the main line of infrastructure, such as water supply, drainage, sewerage/septage, roads, streetlights, electricity, etc.
Plug-and-play industrial parks are pre-developed industrial ecosystems where land, trunk infrastructure, utilities, and common facilities are made available beforehand. In many cases, approvals and basic clearances are
streamlined through single-window systems
. This allows enterprises to move faster from financial decisions to production, while reducing upfront costs and implementation delays.
Such models are becoming more relevant as supply chains diversify across locations and manufacturing becomes more time-sensitive.
Investors increasingly seek locations where land availability, connectivity, utilities, and regulatory processes are predictable
.
The plug-and-play model is already gaining traction in India. In the Union Budget 2025–26,
₹2,500 crore was allocated
for the development of plug-and-play industrial parks. India currently has
260 plug-and-play industrial parks
, reflecting the growing adoption of infrastructure-ready manufacturing ecosystems across sectors and states.
The plug-and-play model is also being extended to sector-specific industrial facilities. In July 2026, the Government approved the
BHAVYA-Rasayan Scheme for three Chemical Parks
. These parks will provide common facilities and environmental safeguards for chemical manufacturing.
Dholera SIR: An Integrated Industrial City
Dholera, Gujarat is emerging as a new-generation industrial city. Wide roads, reliable utilities, digital networks, and modern urban services were planned from the start. Power, water, gas, and drainage systems run through a common underground network,
creating a plug-and-play environment for industries.
The region is developing as a hub for advanced manufacturing sectors.
Semiconductors, aerospace and defence, solar manufacturing, green hydrogen, biotechnology, and heavy engineering
are among the focused sectors. Strong links to ports, airports, expressways, and the Dedicated Freight Corridor connect Dholera to domestic and global markets. Outcomes include:
495 acres
allotted across
11 plots
Investment potential:
₹97,328 crore
Employment potential:
6,000+ jobs
Land has been allotted for major projects, including Tata Electronics' semiconductor facility and Renew Power solar module manufacturing plant.
Towards a New Manufacturing Ecosystem
India’s manufacturing landscape is evolving with greater emphasis on integrated industrial development. The shift from industrial estates to planned manufacturing hubs reflects this changing approach. BHAVYA represents the next step in this transistion. Alongside other initiatives for industrial development, it forms part of India’s broader effort to strengthen its manufacturing base and enhance its role in global manufacturing.

title: NIPER Raebareli and AstraZeneca India Partner to Strengthen Clinical Research Capabilities Across 25 Emerging Geographies
subtitle: Department of Pharmaceuticals Supports NIPER Raebareli–AstraZeneca Collaboration to Advance India’s Clinical Trial Ecosystem Under Biopharma SHAKTI
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Pharmaceuticals
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 3:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
To strengthen India’s clinical research capabilities and expand the country’s participation in global clinical trials,
National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER), Raebareli
, and
AstraZeneca India
have partnered to extend clinical trial capabilities beyond the metros, building a trained workforce and inspection-ready sites in
25 emerging research geographies
across India. The MoU was signed in the presence of
Shri Manoj Joshi, Secretary, Department of Pharmaceuticals
, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers in New Delhi today. This collaboration furthers the vision of
Biopharma SHAKTI
, the Government of India’s flagship initiative to build a stronger biopharma ecosystem, including setting up
1,000 clinical trial sites
across the country.
The collaboration will begin with adopting
25 clinical trial sites,
assessing their capabilities, providing targeted training and mentoring, and strengthening documentation and support processes related to ethics, safety and trial feasibility. The Department of Pharmaceuticals, will provide direction and endorsement, aligning the initiative with national clinical research priorities. Building on this government-led framework, AstraZeneca India will contribute clinical development expertise to design and deliver the programme, engage India and global faculty, and support the participating sites through training, workshops, governance and site-readiness.
In his address,
Shri Manoj Joshi
, Secretary, Department of Pharmaceuticals, stated,
“Our country has the talent and expertise to play a larger role in global clinical trials. Strengthening clinical trials capabilities beyond major metropolitan centres will help expand the pool of skilled professionals and research-ready sites across the country. This collaboration brings together government, academia and industry to strengthen clinical research capabilities in a structured manner and directly advances key objectives of Biopharma SHAKTI.”
Dr. Shubhini Saraf,
Director NIPER Raebareli, highlighted that
“The Centre of Excellence will provide a dedicated platform for structured training and certification in clinical research. By combining academic and industry expertise, NIPER Raebareli will help develop a skilled workforce and create a model that can be expanded to other geographies and therapeutic areas.”
Shri Praveen Rao Akkinepally,
Country President and Managing Director of AstraZeneca Pharma India Limited, stated that “Clinical research is central to bringing innovative medicines to patients. Our collaboration with NIPER Raebareli, with Government support, aims to strengthen India’s clinical research capabilities, expand trial participation and build a sustainable, high-quality research ecosystem.”
The initiative is designed as a scalable national model, with the potential to expand to additional geographies and therapeutic areas beyond oncology following the proof-of-concept phase.

title: Advanced Chemicals, Petrochemicals and Material Technologies Included under Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme
subtitle: Government of India approves the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC) proposal to include the Chemicals and Petrochemicals under RDI Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 OCT 2026 8:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government of India has included Advanced Chemicals, Petrochemicals and Material Technologies as an additional technology area eligible for funding under the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, with effect from 8 October 2026.
The decision has been taken by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, following a proposal by the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.
DCPC had proposed the inclusion of the chemicals and petrochemicals sector as a priority area under the RDI Scheme. The decision is expected to strengthen research, development and innovation in the chemicals and petrochemicals sector and facilitate the development of indigenous technologies for advanced industrial applications.
Under the visionary leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India launched the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme in November 2025, with a corpus of ₹1 lakh crore to catalyse private-sector investment in research, development and innovation. The scheme seeks to provide long-term financing and refinancing on favourable terms for transformative projects, accelerate the adoption of advanced technologies, strengthen India’s industrial competitiveness and foster self-reliance in critical and emerging technology areas.
At the launch of the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme last year, the Prime Minister said, “India is rapidly building a vibrant ecosystem for research and development. We are focusing on Ease of Doing Research so that a modern ecosystem of innovation can flourish in India.”
Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilizers & Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, has welcomed the inclusion of the sector under the RDI Scheme and described it as an important development for the chemicals and petrochemicals industry.
Shri Nadda said the decision would provide a much-needed impetus to research and innovation, supporting the development of advanced, efficient and cost-effective technologies for manufacturing chemicals, petrochemical products, polymers and their derivatives in India.
The inclusion of Advanced Chemicals, Petrochemicals and Material Technologies is aligned with the broader objective of strengthening India's domestic manufacturing ecosystem, promoting technology-led industrial growth and reducing dependence on imported technologies and high-value materials.
